messages:
Maria: Quick sync 1: canary for gpt-small-v2 lands tomorrow. We still need a final take on automatic fallback behavior in the API + Console.
Alex: Ok. Product wants two flows: a simple template-based policy and an advanced explicit chain. We need API shape + how Console surfaces it.
Sophie: UX principle: most users want a short path. Present "safe-mode" levels (strict / normal / flexible) and an optional advanced editor for ordering fallbacks.
Tim: Oncall: previous automatic downgrades led to silent quality regressions. Any flow that downgrades model quality must require explicit opt-in and clear telemetry.
Drew: Infra: regional failover is straightforward. Model-variant fallback requires compatibility checks (quantization, tensor-layout). If incompatible, failover should skip variant and record reason.
Alex: Draft API example (explicit):
```
{
  "canary_pct": 10,
  "fallback_chain": ["local:fast-quant", "remote:standard", "emergency:legacy"],
  "latency_threshold_ms": 1000,
  "quality_floor_pct": 95
}
```
This is an explicit ordered chain.
Sophie: Console should turn that into an ordered list UI with drag-to-reorder and a single "safe-mode" switch that maps to templates.
Maria: How do we compute "quality_floor_pct"? Product expects some built-in signal but teams will want to supply custom evaluation prompts.
Tim: Telemetry requirements: emit a fallback_event for every fallback with reason tags: capacity|latency|error|compatibility|region. Include previous_model, chosen_model, observed_latency_ms, and a short hashed sample of input/output so we can compute regression stats without exposing PII.
Alex: Alternate approach: templates where strictness drives a generated chain. Templates are easiest for self-serve. Example: { "safe_mode": "strict" } => only same-region compatible variants, never a lower-quality fallback.
Drew: Templates + overrides makes sense. Backend should resolve a final policy by merging team template and route-level explicit entries. Merge rules need to be deterministic.
Sophie: Console feature: preview simulation. Run the candidate policy over historical traffic profile (first 5k requests) and show estimated fallback distribution, expected cost delta, and sample outputs. That helps PMs decide.
Maria: Capacity nuance: if canary is on reserved pool, fallback should prefer reserved/dedicated pools before hitting shared. We need fields for preferred_pool and allow_shared_fallback.
Alex: Add fields: preferred_capacity_pool: string, allow_shared_fallback: boolean.
Tim: Safety guard: if more than 4% of requests are served by a lower-quality model for a rolling 10m window, auto-pause the rollout and page oncall. That threshold should be team-configurable.
Drew: We'll implement compatibility-check API. Routing must call sync_check(modelA, modelB) for each candidate pair; if check fails, skip. sync_check must be fast (<20ms) or cached.
Sophie: UI detail: show human-friendly variant labels (e.g., "fast-quant (90% quality)") and a tooltip with perf/quant/size. Avoid internal IDs in the Console.
Maria: Draft decision from this thread: 
- API supports both explicit fallback_chain and template-based safe_mode. explicit chain overrides template.
- Guards: latency_threshold_ms, quality_floor_pct, min_pool_capacity.
- Capacity fields: preferred_capacity_pool and allow_shared_fallback.
- Safety: auto-pause when downgrade_rate_pct > 4% sustained over 10m (configurable per-team).
- Telemetry: emit fallback_event per decision with reason and hashed sample ids.
- Compatibility: routing must perform a synchronous compatibility check; incompatible variants skipped.
Any objections?
Alex: +1. Please add merge semantics doc for template vs explicit (explicit wins), and keep API backwards-compatible.
Tim: +1 if paging thresholds are configurable and documented in runbooks.
Drew: +1; infra will provide the sync_check API and a cached compatibility table.
Sophie: +1 but request product support for the simulation preview (needs compute + UI work).
Jules (Product): Acknowledged, will queue simulation funding for next sprint.
Maria: Action items:
- Alex: OpenAPI patch + three sample policies (strict, default, flexible) by EOD Wednesday.
- Sophie: Mockups for template vs explicit policy flows + preview screen by Thursday.
- Drew: Compatibility sync-check API spec + perf targets by Friday.
- Tim: Runbook stub and alert config for auto-pause behavior.
- Jules: Coordinate simulation compute budget and docs.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: 2028-10-05 09:00 UTC - ensure API freeze window aligns.
Alex: Will coordinate freeze window and sample configs.
Maria: I'll file RFC and attach these notes. If no objections I'll merge decision in RFC tomorrow.
Sophie: tagging @product and design for simulation prioritization :eyes:
Maria: Thanks all :thumbsup:
